source: Hand-tuned for gameplay; capacities and prices loosely based on public launch provider figures and NASA 'Design and Develop Science Missions'

rows: Share a big rocket with dozens of other satellites. Cheap, but you only go where the rocket goes (sun-synchronous orbit). NASA's CubeSat Launch Initiative flies student satellites this way.
A small dedicated rocket. Your own ride to low orbit, and a tiny payload can even reach the Moon. It sent NASA's CAPSTONE to the Moon in 2022.
Launched from under an airplane. Flexible, but expensive for how little it carries. It launched NASA's NuSTAR X-ray telescope in 2012.
Workhorse medium-lift rocket. Reaches every orbit in this game. It launched NASA's TESS planet hunter in 2018.
A very reliable mid-size rocket, NASA's go-to for science. It launched LRO to the Moon (2009) and MAVEN to Mars (2013).
Heavy lifter for big spacecraft headed to high orbits or the Moon. Its first flight (2024) carried NASA instruments on the Peregrine Moon lander.
Three Falcon 9 cores strapped together: huge capacity for its price. It launched NASA's Psyche (2023) and Europa Clipper (2024).
NASA's Moon rocket. Enormous capacity and an enormous price tag. It flew Artemis I around the Moon in 2022.
